text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli Intelligence tells Prime Minister Netanyahu probability of war with Syria no longer low.
- Bank of Israeli Governor Frenkel opposes taxing savings.
- Senior officials in defence establishment: Israel Aircraft Industries effectively bankrupt.
- B'Tselem human rights group says Israeli army prevents Palestinians from using new Bethlehem bypass road.
- Sharp confrontation between Bank of Israel and Treasury over capital markets reform report.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syrian President Assad, in message to U.S., says Israel has nothing to fear.
- Defence Minister Mordechai to present Hebron redeployment plan to Palestinian President Arafat this evening.
- Government to reject substantial part of the capital markets reform report.
MAARIV
- Calming messages between Syria and Israel.
- Central bank governor could announce at the end of month a 0.8 percentage point drop in interest rates.
- Israel Aircraft Industries owes suppliers more than $200 million.
GLOBES
- Director-general of prime minister's office: I will not endorse savings tax.
- Most members of parliament's finance committee oppose recommendations to tax savings.
- State of Israel Properties to tender state holdings in United Mizrahi Bank in early 1997.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime minister: We won't be pressured by Syria.
- Brodet Committee proposes taxing short-term savings.
- Illegal Jerusalem Old City dwelling demolished.
